evidence.quote: There is no restriction on target dimension or on how the map is computed.

exclusions.query: Efficient production implementation of the upper embedding
exclusions.reason: The distortion theorem supplies a finite-dimensional map without a runtime or memory guarantee.

exclusions.query: Lower distortion preservation by the direct binary substitutions for unequal input lengths
exclusions.reason: The lower assertion is restricted to equal input lengths.

hypotheses.statement:
There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and an integer $d_0$ such that, for every integer $d\geq d_0$ and every finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with $|\Sigma|\geq2$, $$\label{eq:main}
 \exp\!\bigl(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\bigr)
 \leq E_\Sigma(d)\leq
 \exp\!\bigl(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\bigr).$$ Each of our two lower constructions supplies a binary subset whose words have one common length at most $d$ and whose least $\ell_1$ distortion satisfies the lower bound. The upper bound is realized by a deterministic finite-dimensional map.

For all finite words $x,y$, $$q(x,y)\leq\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\leq2q(x,y),\qquad
 \operatorname{ED}(x,y)\leq |x|+|y|-2\operatorname{LCS}(x,y)\leq2\operatorname{ED}(x,y).$$ The middle expression in the second comparison is the insertion–deletion distance. In particular, $r_n\leq\operatorname{ED}\leq2r_n$ at equal length.

For all sufficiently large $h$, $$\label{mask:reset-bound}
 D_h(1/2)\geq4^{-h}h^{-h/2-O(\sqrt h)-4h/100},$$ with an absolute implicit constant.

For $f:X\to\ell_1$ with $X$ finite, there are nonnegative coefficients $a_A$ on the nonempty proper subsets of $X$ such that $$\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1=\sum_A a_A\delta_A(x,y),\qquad
 \sum_Aa_A\leq\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset X}\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1.$$

If $\chi_\alpha|_{C_h}=1$ and $\chi_\alpha(w)\ne1$, then $$\label{mask:weight}
 \sum_{i=1}^r|\alpha_i|\geq B.$$

For $0\le\ell\le h$, put $$F_\ell=m^{-\ell/4-100m^{3/4}}.$$ For all sufficiently large $m$, the following holds for every $0\le\ell\le h$. If $z\in\mathbb T$ is nonzero, has finite order $q\le m^{10}$, and satisfies $\gcd(q,\prod_{a=1}^{\ell}P_a)=1$, then $$\label{eq:exc-phase-lower}
 \rho_\ell(z)\ge F_\ell.$$ The empty product in the case $\ell=0$ is one.

If $\xi\in H^\perp$ and $\chi_\xi(w_*)\ne1$, then $$\label{eq:exc-annihilator-threshold}
 T(\xi)\ge K,\qquad K=m^{3h/4}.$$

Let $c_0,C_0>0$ be fixed. Suppose that for every sufficiently large integer $k$ there is an integer $n_k\geq1$ and a finite subset of $\{0,1\}^{n_k}$ whose least $\ell_1$ distortion is at least $\exp(c_0k\log k)$, where $\log n_k\leq C_0k^2\log k$. Then there are constants $c>0$ and $d_0$, depending only on $c_0,C_0$ and the starting threshold, such that for every integer $d\geq d_0$ a binary subset of one length at most $d$ has distortion at least $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$.

There are absolute constants $C>0$ and $d_0\ge3$ such that, for every finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with $|\Sigma|\ge2$ and every integer $d\ge d_0$, there are an integer $M\ge1$ and a deterministic map $F:\Sigma^{\le d}\longrightarrow\ell_1^M$ satisfying $$\operatorname{ED}(x,y)\le \|F(x)-F(y)\|_1
 \le \exp\!\bigl(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\bigr)
       \operatorname{ED}(x,y)
 \qquad(x,y\in\Sigma^{\le d}).$$ Here $\ell_1^M$ is real, and both $C$ and $d_0$ are independent of $\Sigma$.

Two words of length $n\ge0$ can be joined by exactly $r_n(x,y)$ moves, each deleting one symbol and inserting one symbol while preserving length $n$. For a single move, restrictions to any common interval of $a$ positions have deficit at most one, and hence edit distance at most two.*

*For a fixed partition of the positions into nonempty consecutive blocks, at most two blocks contain a deletion or insertion endpoint. In any other block of length $m$, the two subwords agree, or the prefix of length $m-1$ of one agrees with the suffix of length $m-1$ of the other.

coverage.checked_domain: All binary endpoint pairs of lengths at most 3; every common padding length from the longer endpoint through 5; explicit empty, unequal-length, identical and substitution boundary cases.
